title: Robinhood Expands Tokenized Stock Trading to More Than 120 Countries

tickers.name: Robinhood Markets, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
CEO Vlad Tenev told the 'Sources' podcast that the shift to tokenize equities is a permanent development in the financial industry and is not reversible. Tenev argued that letting users trade stock tokens, which generally lack voting rights, allows companies to attract fresh capital from a global pool of investors. The retail broker also noted that more than 100,000 customers have already begun using its AI agent for automated trading.

The remarks follow a public campaign against stock tokenization, highlighted by a full-page advertisement in the Wall Street Journal. Ahead of Robinhood's Oct. 27 earnings call, data suggests its Robinhood Chain earned more than $40M in revenue and handled $85B in decentralized exchange volume last quarter. Tokenized assets on the network total more than $330M, with $130M in those holdings consisting of equities.

Robinhood’s CEO on letting AI trade your money

@vladtenev on Robinhood’s new agent bet and the AI ownership inequality problem.

Robinhood wants to put an AI hedge fund in your pocket. CEO Vlad Tenev tells me how Robinhood Agents brings AI trading into the app, and why he expects agents to generate a growing share of individual investors’ trading activity.

We discuss how much control to give an AI that can trade your money, why Robinhood keeps agents in separate accounts, and where investors will find an edge when everyone has access to powerful models. He also explains his push for every Robinhood employee to have agents working while they sleep.

Tenev argues that the AI backlash is partly an ownership problem: most people can’t invest in the companies driving it. We get into Robinhood’s push to open private markets to everyday investors, the coming AI IPOs, and his response to criticism of tokenized stocks. We also discuss prediction markets and why he objects to AI labs keeping their most powerful tools to themselves.
